The most recent U.S. President to visit Iceland was Joe Biden. He attended the NATO summit in Riga, Latvia, in June 2023, and made a brief stop in Iceland on his way back to the United States. However, this was a technical stopover rather than an official state visit.

The last U.S. President to make an official visit to Iceland was Bill Clinton in May 2000. During his visit, he met with then-President of Iceland, Ólafur Ragnar Grímsson, and discussed various bilateral and international issues.

If you're looking for the most recent official state visit, it would be Bill Clinton's in 2000.

There have been a few instances of U.S. Presidents visiting Iceland. Some notable examples include:

1. 1950: President Harry S. Truman visited Iceland to inspect the Keflavik Naval Air Station in August 1950.
2. 1957: President Dwight D. Eisenhower visited Iceland in August 1957. 
3. 1976: President Jimmy Carter visited Iceland in October 1976 to attend the annual Arctic Council meeting.
4. 2015: President Barack Obama visited Iceland on April 8-9, 2016.

Barack Obama briefly visited Iceland's Keflavik Airport in 2016 while making a refueling stop on Air Force One. However, this wasn't considered an official state visit. The last U.S. President to make an official visit to Iceland was Ronald Reagan in 1986, when he met with Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev for the Reykjavik Summit.
